what: Sankaracharya math: named first of the chief Saiva maths near Swarga-dwar, with a fine library of old manuscripts. This is the only statement on it in the main account (Govardhana is not named).
quote: The chief Saiva maths are located in the sandy tract near Swarga-dwar, Tiz., Sankara eharya, with a fine library of old manuscripts

what: Gazetteer article on Puri: the Sankaracharya math is said to have been founded by Sankaracharya himself, evidently of considerable age (surrounded by sand dune); library of about 1,200 manuscripts, some 300 to 400 years old; stands near the Kabirpanthi math and near Haridasa's reputed grave.
quote: The latter math is said to have been founded by Sankaraoharya himself, and is evidently of considerable age

what: Hindu sects at Jagannath (quoting N. K. Bose, Calcutta Review 1891): the learned pandit of the Sankaracharya monastery seeks salvation by spiritual knowledge; also many Saiva sannyasis enduring austerities. Shows the math as the Advaita/jnana representative among sects.
quote: There you see the learned pandit of the Sankaracharya monastery seeking salvation by. the way of spiritual knowledge.

what: Followers of Sankaracharya listed first among sects doing homage to Jagannath, with Ramanuja, Ramananda, Kabir, Chaitanya and Nanak; all sects united by belief in Jagannath's supremacy.
quote: The followers of Sankaraoharya, Eamanuja, Eamanand, Kabir, Ohaitanya and Nanak are to be seen doing homage to the great god.

what: Saiva sannyasis present at Jagannath voluntarily enduring severe austerity (order not named, called Saiva sannyasis).
quote: Here you find a large number of Saiva sannyam voluntarily enduring excruciating torture and misery, and seeking absorption into the deity by severe austerities.

what: Sankarananda math: the other chief Saiva math, with a branch at Bhubaneswar. Likely Saiva/Sannyasi but its order is not stated.
quote: and Sankarananda, which has a branch at Bhubaneswar.

what: Five maths, all non-Vaishnavite, the inmates Saivas and Sannyasis. No names; Sankarananda has a branch there (see Puri). Sannyasi here is the only use of the word in the volume.

what: Small math of the Kabirpanthis (followers of Kabir and Guru Nanak) near the Sankaracharya math; Kabirpanthi math prominent among those round Swarga-dwara.

what: Definition: maths are monastic houses for feeding travellers, beggars and ascetics and instructing chelas; heads (Mahants or Mathadharis) elected from chelas, assisted by Adhikaris; generally celibate, but in some maths married men hold office; mahants are gurus with money and land endowments. Both Saiva and Vaishnava maths exist.

what: Vaishnava math lands are amruta-manohi (to supply bhoga before Jagannath, mahaprasad given to pilgrims, beggars, ascetics); income of 29 maths from land Rs 1,45,400 in 1848.
quote: The lands of the latter are known as amruta-manohi (literally nectar-food)

what: Richest Vaishnava math (Ramanandi/Ramat inmates). 18th-century Mahant a famed holy ascetic with large offerings. Mahant is a major zamindar: ryots find him a better landlord than old families; four-anna share of Kotdesh estate bought at 1896 auction; carved doorway praised by Havell.
quote: the Mahant of the Emar Math in the 18th century, who had the reputation of being a very holy ascetic, similarly got large offerings from his followers.

what: Mahant of Emar Math is a landlord (Settlement Officer McPherson: ryots find a better friend in him than in effete old families); purchased a four-annas share of the Kotdesh estate at the 1896 auction.
quote: The ryots find a better friend in such landlords as the Mahant of the Emar Math

what: Ramanandi math (Sriramadasa = Dakhinaparsva); abbot was guru of the Maratha Governor and received rich Maratha endowments. Named among the richest.
